jobs.name: stand_m3100
jobs.note: Retry at 3072. The 4096 attempt died on CUDA error 600 - the video renderer needs its own GPU memory. Does the 3100 g robot hold itself up?

jobs.name: walk_m3100_a
jobs.note: The main event. First walk on the 3100 g robot, task defaults untouched. Everything else tonight is measured against this.

jobs.name: walk_m3100_b
jobs.note: Same as A but leg_swing 1.0 -> 1.8. Tests whether a heavier robot needs to be paid more to actually swing its legs rather than creep on stiff ones.

jobs.name: walk_m3100_f
jobs.note: Targets what walk_a actually failed on. It covered 6.03 m with 0 of 64 falling, then drifted 3487 mm sideways against a 100 mm bar. wandering -1 to -4 makes leaving the line four times more expensive; track_turn 1 to 2 pays harder for holding the commanded yaw of zero. veering cannot be set from the CLI - the curriculum overwrites it at step 0.
jobs.command: python scripts/train.py Gray-Walk --num-envs 3072 --iterations 3000 --name walk_m3100_f --reward wandering=-4.0 --reward track_turn=2.0

jobs.name: walk_m3100_g
jobs.note: Tests the TURN_STD fix, 0.30 -> 0.80. walk_a and walk_b both walked over 5 m without falling and then drifted 3.5-4 m sideways, because track_turn paid 1.4e-11 at the yaw error they actually made - a dead term with no gradient. This is the first run where the policy is actually told to stop spinning. No weight overrides: the point is to see the fix alone.

jobs.name: walk_m3100_c
jobs.note: Same as A but speed tracking and ground covered weighted harder. Tests whether the extra 1070 g makes the robot trade distance away to stay safe.
jobs.command: python scripts/train.py Gray-Walk --num-envs 3072 --iterations 3000 --name walk_m3100_c --reward track_speed=3.0 --reward ground_covered=1.5

jobs.name: walk_m3100_h
jobs.note: Tests the new landing_speed term alone. Charges a foot for how fast it is still travelling downward at the instant it touches down - the owner asked for the leg to ease in at the end of its movement rather than run into the floor. Deliberately 3072 robots and no reward overrides, so it matches walk_g exactly and the landing term is the ONLY difference. Changing the robot count too would make the result unreadable.

jobs.name: walk_m3100_h
jobs.note: Landing-speed term, at 6400 robots. NOTE the confound: walk_g and walk_c ran at 3072, so this differs from them by the new term AND by robot count. 6400 is the owner call - the card was sitting at 7.8 of 12 GB and idle capacity is worse than a slightly muddier comparison. walk_d follows at 6400 with no new term, which recovers the clean A/B.

jobs.name: walk_m3100_h
